sections.h2: Selling a house in Eau Claire
sections.html:
Eau Claire is the seat of Eau Claire County, where the Eau Claire and Chippewa rivers meet. The July 2025 estimate is 72,465 residents, up 4.4% from the 2020 base. Renters outnumber owners here, so many sales involve tenants, small multifamily buildings or houses near the university. Part of the city lies in Chippewa County, so if your parcel is on that side of the line, ask which county's Register of Deeds and treasurer handle your recording and tax bill.

Whether you list, sell by owner or sell to a cash buyer, four things decide how smoothly it goes: city permit records, the assessment and tax calendar, the seller disclosure report, and recording the deed with the county.

Barely more than half of Eau Claire homes are owner-occupied, so rentals are a large part of what changes hands. The older neighborhoods, including the Randall Park, Third Ward and Emery Street Bungalow historic districts, add bungalows and large lumber-era houses to the resale market.

Before you advertise, ask the Eau Claire Area School District office which school an address feeds, and do the same for parcels near the edge of the city, which may sit in a different district.

The City of Eau Claire uses January 1 as its assessment date. The tax bill is due in full by January 31, or in two installments on January 31 and July 31. Notices of assessment change usually go out between the end of April and the end of May, and the Board of Review meets in a 45-day window that opens on the fourth Monday in April.

  • Talk to an assessor first. The city says that informal meeting shows how your value was set.
  • If you still disagree, you can appeal the Board's decision to the Department of Revenue within 20 days of receiving it, with a $100 filing fee, when the value in dispute is $1 million or less.
  • A court appeal must be filed within 90 days after the Board of Review adjourns, and it is decided on the record from your hearing.

You can reach the assessor's office at 715-839-4926 and search property records in the city's Beacon tool. Because tax is billed for the whole year, your closing prorates it between you and the buyer, and the title company can show the split. Ask the Eau Claire County treasurer for the status of any unpaid bill on the parcel.

Inspection Services reviews plans, issues permits and inspects construction and remodeling covering building, heating, air conditioning, electrical and plumbing. It also enforces ordinances on floodplain, zoning, property upkeep and land use. Requests go through the Evolve portal or by phone, not by email to individual inspectors.

Short-term rentals have separate rules that shape how a buyer can use the house. Chapter 5.66 created a Short-Term Rental License.

  • First apply for a Tourist Rooming House license through the city-county Health Department (715-839-4718).
  • Planning and Zoning (715-839-4914) reviews the city license, with a parking count, a building plan and a trash container sketch.
  • The initial review fee is $700 and annual renewal is $300, with licenses running from June 30 to June 30.

If your house has operated as a short-term rental, confirm the license status with Planning before you list, since buyers who want to continue the use will ask.

sections.h2: Transferring a deed in Eau Claire County
sections.html:
The Eau Claire County Register of Deeds records deeds, mortgages, satisfactions, plats and certified survey maps. Since January 1, 2025 a postage-paid envelope must be supplied for return of paper documents. The county's land records page has forms, the electronic transfer return, a recording checklist and the filing fee schedule, and you can reach the office at rod@eauclairecounty.gov.

Wis. Stat. 77.22 charges the grantor 30 cents for each $100 of value, and the register collects it when the deed is submitted. The register has no duty to check the value you report. For a gift or a deed with nominal consideration, Wis. Stat. 77.21 uses the estimated open-market price, which matters when a family member buys at a discount.

sections.h2: What the Wisconsin disclosure rule requires
sections.html:
Chapter 709 requires owners of one-to-four-unit property to hand the buyer a completed condition report within 10 days after the contract is accepted. In a condominium sale the owner also supplies an addendum with condominium information at the same time. A buyer who does not receive the report can rescind within two business days after the 10 days run out and recover deposits.

Personal representatives, trustees, conservators and court-supervised fiduciaries who never lived in the house are excused. The excusal is limited to those fiduciaries, so an ordinary owner, including a landlord, completes the report.

A listing works when the house shows well and you can handle showings and a lender's timeline. A cash sale fits a house with deferred repairs, a tenant in place, a probate timeline or a payoff date.

Ask for a net sheet with any offer. It should list the loan payoff, the $3 per $1,000 transfer fee, recording, prorated tax and repair credits, so the offers compare on proceeds.

faqs.q: Who records deeds for Eau Claire properties?
faqs.a: The Eau Claire County Register of Deeds. Provide a postage-paid return envelope for paper documents, and ask the office for its current filing fee schedule before you submit.

faqs.q: When are Eau Claire property taxes due?
faqs.a: January 31 in full, or in two installments on January 31 and July 31. The assessment date is January 1.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer fee on an Eau Claire sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays 30 cents per $100 of value under Wis. Stat. 77.22.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to run a short-term rental in Eau Claire?
faqs.a: Yes. Eau Claire requires a Tourist Rooming House license from the Health Department and a city Short-Term Rental License, with a $700 initial review fee and a $300 annual renewal.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Eau Claire assessment after the Board of Review?
faqs.a: Yes. You can appeal to the Wisconsin Department of Revenue within 20 days of the decision, with a $100 filing fee, or to circuit court within 90 days after the Board adjourns.
